speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and the classic signs of obstructive jaundice with weight loss, I need to rule out pancreatic cancer. Have you noticed a lump in the epigastric area or pain that specifically radiates to your back? REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of the Abdomen with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is unexpected; the CT scan showing normal readings makes a pancreatic obstruction highly unlikely. However, your symptoms of pale stools and dark urine confirm a blockage or severe dysfunction. Did that episode of abdominal pain three years ago involve jaundice or elevated liver enzymes at the time? Also, have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin in the past month?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) or Cholangiocarcinoma. The normal CT scan rules out a mass obstructing the pancreatic head, but your classic obstructive symptoms (pale stools, dark urine, pruritus, weight loss) combined with your age and history suggest a stricture in the bile ducts. Since the ultrasound and CT were normal, I suspect the blockage might be in the intrahepatic ducts or missed on imaging. I need to see the MRCP or ERCP images to visualize the biliary tree specifically. REQUEST IMAGES: MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography).
